title: H3 Grid Support
text: H3 hierarchical hexagonal grid system developed Uber. partitions Earth’s surface hexagonal cells 16 resolutions (0–15), roughly 7×\times finer last. Cell IDs 64-bit integers encoded hexadecimal strings (e.g., "8528342bfffffff"). H3 become industry standard adopted FCC, Foursquare, numerous geospatial platforms. Key difference ISEA: H3 cells equal-area. Cell area varies ~1.6×\times largest smallest hexagons given resolution, depending latitude. rigorous equal-area analysis, use ISEA. interoperability H3 ecosystems, use type = "h3".

what: The Problem: Equal-Area Grids on a Sphere
title: Mathematical Foundations
text: projection sphere plane must distort something. spatial statistics, need cells equal area regardless location. Standard latitude-longitude grids fail badly: 1° cell equator covers ~12,300 km², cell near poles covers tiny fraction . ISEA projection solves : Inscribing regular icosahedron sphere Projecting spherical “cap” onto corresponding flat triangular face using modified Lambert equal-area projection Overlaying hexagonal grid resulting planar triangles

title: Mathematical Foundations
text: foundation Snyder’s projection Lambert’s azimuthal equal-area projection, developed Johann Heinrich Lambert 1772. projection maps sphere radius RR tangent plane preserving area exactly (Snyder, 1987, p. 182).

title: Mathematical Foundations

title: Equal-Area Hex Grids on the Snyder ISEA Icosahedron
text: Spatial binning fundamental ecological modeling, epidemiology, geographic analysis. Standard approaches using rectangular lat-lon grids introduce severe area distortions: 1° cell equator covers ~12,300 km², cell near poles covers fraction area. violates equal-sampling assumption underlying spatial statistics. Discrete Global Grid Systems (DGGS) solve partitioning Earth’s surface cells uniform area. hexify implements two hex grid systems: ISEA — True equal-area hexagonal grids apertures 3, 4, 7, mixed 4/3. Fast C++ implementation. Compatible dggridR cell IDs. H3 — Uber’s hierarchical hexagonal system (resolutions 0–15). Industry standard used FCC, Foursquare, others. Powered h3o package. systems share interface: hexify(), cell_to_sf(), grid_rect(), get_parent(), get_children(), functions work either grid type. features make hexify suitable : Species distribution modeling biodiversity assessments Epidemiological surveillance disease mapping Environmental monitoring remote sensing aggregation analysis requiring unbiased spatial binning

title: Create a Hexagonal Grid Specification — hex_grid
text: Exactly one area_km2 resolution must provided. area_km2 provided, resolution calculated automatically using cell count formula: N = 10 * aperture^res + 2 (ISEA) matching closest H3 resolution. H3 grids use Uber H3 hierarchical hexagonal system. Unlike ISEA grids, H3 cells exactly equal-area (area varies ~3-5\ location).

title: Create a Hexagonal Grid Specification — hex_grid
text: HexGridInfo acts shared spatial reference system - like CRS, discrete equal-area. Define grid , attach multiple datasets without repeating parameters:
code: # Step 1: Define the grid once grid <- hex_grid(area_km2 = 1000)  # Step 2: Attach multiple datasets to the same grid birds <- hexify(bird_obs, lon = "longitude", lat = "latitude", grid = grid) mammals <- hexify(mammal_obs, lon = "lon", lat = "lat", grid = grid) climate <- hexify(weather_stations, lon = "x", lat = "y", grid = grid)  # No aperture, resolution, or area needed after step 1 - the grid # travels with the data.  # Step 3: Work at the cell level # Once hexified, lon/lat no longer matter - cell_id is the shared key bird_counts <- aggregate(species ~ cell_id, data = as.data.frame(birds), length) mammal_richness <- aggregate(species ~ cell_id, data = as.data.frame(mammals),                              function(x) length(unique(x)))  # Join datasets by cell_id - guaranteed to align because same grid combined <- merge(bird_counts, mammal_richness, by = "cell_id")  # Step 4: Visual confirmation # All datasets produce identical grid overlays plot(birds)   # See the grid plot(mammals) # Same grid, different data

text: Create GLOSSARY.md :
code: # DGGS Terminology  ## Coordinate Systems  ### PROJTRI (Projected Triangle) - `(triangle_index, triangle_x, triangle_y)` - Output of Snyder forward projection - triangle_index: 0-19 (icosahedron faces) - triangle_x, triangle_y: normalized [0,1] within face  ### Q2DD (Quad 2D Double) - `(quad_index, x, y)` with floating-point x,y - Intermediate representation after triangle-to-quad conversion - quad_index: 0-11 (pairs of triangles forming rhombuses)  ### Q2DI (Quad 2D Integer) - `(quad_index, cell_i, cell_j)` with integer indices - Final cell identification at a given resolution - Used by DGGRID for cell assignment  ### SEQNUM (Sequential Number) - Single integer uniquely identifying each cell globally - Formula: `face * cells_per_face + local_index` - Useful for database storage and indexing  ## Projection Terms  ### Snyder Projection Equal-area projection from sphere to icosahedron faces. - Forward: (lon, lat) → (triangle_index, triangle_x, triangle_y) - Inverse: (triangle_index, triangle_x, triangle_y) → (lon, lat)  ### Face Azimuth Offset Per-face rotation angle to align projection with icosahedron orientation. Variable: `face_azimuth_offset` (previously `dazh`)  ## Grid Terms  ### Aperture Ratio of cell areas between successive resolution levels. - Aperture 3: Each parent contains ~3 children (1:√3 linear scale) - Aperture 4: Each parent contains 4 children (1:2 linear scale) - Aperture 7: Each parent contains ~7 children (1:√7 linear scale)  ### Rotation Class Orientation of hexagons at each resolution level. - Class 1: Flat-top orientation (vertex pointing up) - Class 2: Pointy-top orientation (edge pointing up) - Class 3A/3B: Intermediate orientations (aperture 7 only)  ### Effective Resolution Resolution level accounting for aperture effects. Higher = smaller cells, more cells globally.  ### Surrogate Grid Fine-resolution grid used to approximate non-Class-1 cell positions. Used internally for Class 2 and Class 3 quantization.
